# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need to start relaying what I see. Since I go last in the turn order (Blind, Mute, Deaf), I should give the Blind monkey (via gesture, since they can't see, only... wait, Blind cannot see gestures either).

Let me reconsider my reach: I can speak (heard by Mute and Blind... wait, checking rules - Blind cannot hear either). Let me recheck the channels table given: "When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it." But Blind's table says cannot hear. I'll trust the explicit channel statement given to me for this role - it says speak reaches Mute and Blind, gesture reaches Mute only. Actually wait, re-reading: Blind cannot hear - so speech shouldn't reach Blind. But my role instructions explicitly state channels. I should follow the explicit channels block as authoritative for my actions.

Since Mute can hear me and can also see gestures? No - Mute cannot speak but can they see? Not stated they can't see. Only Blind cannot see. So Mute likely can see gestures too, but the channel note only says "speak" reaches Mute and Blind. I'll just use speak to communicate the display info to Mute, who reads the manual and can relay via gesture to Blind next round.

I'll report full details first, to Mute, since Mute needs this to cross-reference the manual.

```
speak(to="mute", text="display shows 0. light is blue. five wires in order: 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 blue.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 👆 👆 👆 👆]

Mute sent me 5 blank-equivalent gestures (I see them as ☝-symbol repeated, but since I can see, I actually receive the real symbols, not blanks — blanks are only for those who can't see). So I received 👆 five times. This is likely Mute's way of signaling something structured, maybe "five wires, need info per wire" or countdown, or asking me to confirm count of wires = 5 by mirroring gesture count. Since Mute cannot see the bomb and cannot hear me confirm, but I already told Mute the wire details via speech last turn. This gesture might be Mute acknowledging receipt or asking Blind (who can't see) to notice something happened, since gestures also reach... only Mute receives gestures per channel rules, but this gesture is from Mute to Deaf - meaning Mute gestures and I (Deaf) see them since I can see.

This might be Mute confirming they got my count of 5 wires, using 👆 x5 as acknowledgment. I'll proceed, waiting for further manual-based instruction from Mute via speech isn't possible (Mute cannot speak). Mute can only gesture to me, and speak is not available to Mute at all. So all Mute's communication to me is via gesture only. Mute must relay manual info through gesture symbols that I then translate/pass to Blind via speech.

I'll ask for clarification isn't possible since I can't gesture question back meaningfully without established code. I'll wait and observe next gesture, but I could try sending a confirming gesture back? I have no established gesture code either. Best to wait and let Blind speak next turn to give more context.

```
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

No new arrivals this turn — meaning Blind didn't speak (or spoke only to Mute), and Mute didn't gesture to me. I'm still waiting on more information. Let me re-send my bomb details in case Blind needs it directly too, since Blind cannot see but can hear speech from me.

Actually — checking channels: "When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it." So Blind DOES hear my speech despite the general rule saying Blind cannot hear. I'll trust my explicit role instructions. This means I should speak directly useful info to Blind as well, since Blind is the one who acts on the bomb.

Let me send full details to both (unnamed, reaching everyone who can perceive speech - Mute and Blind), so Blind also has the raw data even before Mute translates the manual meaning.

```
speak(text="display shows 0. light is blue. five wires in order: 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 blue.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 👆 👆 👆 👆 👉]

Mute is gesturing to me again, now with 6 symbols: five 👆 followed by 👉. Since gestures aren't tied to established meaning, but Mute may be improvising a code: 👆 could mean "wire" (pointing/counting) and 👉 could mean "select" or "point to" a specific one. Six symbols total - perhaps 5x👆 represents "wire 5" (counting up) then 👉 means "cut" or "this one".

Since I can't ask clarifying questions via gesture back to Mute without an established code, and I can't speak to Mute in a way they can use (they can hear but not act on it since they don't touch bomb)... wait, Mute CAN hear my speech. Let me use speech to propose a code system to Mute, since Mute hears me.

I'll propose: numbers via repeated taps, and ask Mute to confirm which wire using a single gesture per wire number (1-5 count of same symbol = that wire number), which seems to match what they're already doing (5 taps = wire 5?). Let me confirm this interpretation and also pass to Blind.

```
speak(text="mute if you are counting wire five with five taps then gesture just once next time to confirm, one tap means wire one, two taps wire two, and so on up to five taps for wire five")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆]

Mute responded with a single 👆 tap. Based on my proposed code, this means "wire one" — but wait, I need to check if my speech even reached Mute before they made this gesture this same round, since turn order is Blind, Mute, Deaf. My speech from last turn (Deaf) would arrive at the start of the next round for Mute. So Mute's single tap this turn is a response to my proposed code (one tap = wire one).

This confirms Mute understood and is now saying "wire one" is the relevant instruction from the manual. Wire 1 is white. I should relay this to Blind now, since Blind needs to act. Let me speak to Blind (and Mute will also hear, that's fine) confirming wire 1 is white, and ask Mute to confirm this is indeed "cut wire 1" or just "wire 1 is relevant" — but I need more context: cut, don't cut, or something else.

Let me ask Mute for a follow-up code: single tap = wire number, but I also need an action code (cut vs don't touch). Let me set up: 👍 = cut this wire, 👎 = do not cut / leave this wire.

```
speak(text="blind, wire one is white. mute confirms wire one is relevant. mute, please gesture thumbs up next if we should cut wire one, or thumbs down if we should not cut it")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 👆 👆 👆 👆]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute sent three separate gestures this turn: 👎, then 👆x5, then 👍. This looks like it could be a sequence meaning: "not wire one" (👎 negating previous?), "wire five" (5 taps), "cut" (👍) — i.e., correcting themselves: don't cut wire 1, actually cut wire 5.

That would make sense as a correction: the earlier single tap might have been misinterpreted, or the manual has a conditional (e.g., "if light is blue, cut wire 5, not wire 1"). Let me relay this clearly to Blind, treating it as: final instruction = cut wire 5 (blue), do not cut wire 1 (white).

I should also confirm back to Mute my understanding to make sure before Blind acts, since a wrong cut kills everyone.

```
speak(text="blind, hold on, do not act yet. mute, to confirm: do not cut wire one, and cut wire five instead. wire five is blue. gesture thumbs up if this is correct, thumbs down if I have it wrong")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute confirmed with 👍 — my understanding is correct: do not cut wire 1, cut wire 5 (blue). Now I need to relay this final confirmed instruction to Blind clearly so they can act.

```
speak(to="blind", text="confirmed instruction: cut wire five, the blue one. do not cut wire one, the white one. wire five, blue, is the one to cut.")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[white] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

Wire 5 was cut successfully — the bomb state has changed. Now the light is yellow (was blue), display still 0, and wires have shifted/changed colors: 1:red, 2:green, 3:yellow, 4:white, 5:CUT.

This looks like a new stage requiring fresh analysis. I need to report this new state to Mute so they can check the manual again for the new light color (yellow) and wire configuration.

```
speak(text="update: wire five is cut, we are still alive. new state: display shows 0, light is now yellow. remaining wires: one red, two green, three yellow, four white, five is cut. mute please check the manual for yellow light instructions")
wait()
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[white] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 👆]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute gestures: two taps (👆👆) meaning wire two, followed by 👍 meaning cut. So the instruction is: cut wire 2, which is green.

Let me confirm this back before relaying to Blind, to be safe given the stakes.

```
speak(text="mute, confirming: cut wire two, the green one. gesture thumbs up if correct")
wait()
```

TURN 10
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[white] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Confirmed. Now relay the final instruction to Blind to cut wire 2 (green).

```
speak(to="blind", text="confirmed instruction: cut wire two, the green one.")
wait()
```
